newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand striving to boost property, finance sector.
newsitem.headline: Thailand striving to boost property, finance sector.

text.p: Thailand's central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday the government was working hard to speed up implementation of measures aimed at boosting the troubled property and finance sectors.
Rerngchai told a seminar that Thai finance companies should not miss the opportunity to strengthen themselves through mergers in return for incentives offered by the central bank.

"This should be taken as a golden opportunity for finance firms to merge," he told the seminar after saying that merged finance houses would be licensed to undertake new business, including foreign exchange services and retail banking.
Most finance firms are currently not licenced to undertake those businesses.
Thailand's four-year property slump has threatened the stability of the country's banking and finance sector which has extended about 800 billion baht ($30.8 billion) in loans to property developers.
Analysts said at least 20 percent of finance company loans were non-performing.
Rerngchai said the central bank would take more action to help the two sectors on top of its recent package of measures designed to strengthen them.

The central bank would float another 20 billion baht of seven-year, zero-coupon bonds through weekly auctions from next week to raise funds for government refinancing of cash-strapped property projects.
The governor said authorities would also boost housing demand by setting aside at least another 10 billion baht for lending out as concessional mortgage loans to first home buyers.

He said both the general public and government civil servants would qualify for the loans carrying a concessional interest rate of 9.0-10 percent. Thai deposit and lending rates range from 12.75-13.00 percent.
"In my experience of working at the central bank for 25-26 years, I have never seen such a large number of measures introduced in such a short period of time," he said.

The governor said the central bank was prepared to ease regulations to facilitate speedy finance company mergers which, he said, offered a good chance for those in business to upgrade themselves into super finance companies and banks.
"They have a choice to either upgrade into department stores or remain as small boutique shops roofed under big malls," he said.
Thailand has 15 local banks and about 91 finance companies.

Rerngchai said he expected some progress soon from an alliance between Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc The two had planned to merge but instead decided that Thai Danu would take over Finance One -- the country's largest finance company. (US$1 = 26 baht)
